description: A forward operating base commander must publish the next day's generator and facility-power plan, assigning the two available generators across the water plant, clinic, and communications annex while setting the fuel reserve and recording the coordination actions required before the plan begins.

shared_context.S1: The base has two serviceable generators available for tomorrow: G-1 is rated for 60 kilowatts and G-2 is rated for 40 kilowatts.
shared_context.S2: The water plant, clinic, and communications annex all require scheduled generator support tomorrow.
shared_context.S3: The base has 1,200 liters of generator fuel on hand at 1700 today.
shared_context.S4: Col. Mercer publishes the final power plan and fuel-control instructions.
shared_context.S5: The base's routine 1700 facilities synchronization requires the facilities, medical, signal, and logistics representatives to report any changes before the commander signs the next-day plan.

PF1.text: Maj. Alvarez confirmed this afternoon that the water plant's morning startup pump draws 55 kilowatts from 0600 to 0800, so the plant must use G-1 during that window; the updated load reading is still in the facilities worksheet and has not been added to the command brief.

PF2.text: Lt. Brooks confirmed today that the clinic's temperature-controlled medication freezer must remain continuously powered by G-2 from 0000 through 2400 tomorrow; the medical equipment notice is awaiting entry in the facility support log.

PF3.text: Capt. Shah confirmed that the communications annex UPS maintenance crew will disconnect its normal feed from 1300 to 1500 tomorrow and requires a G-1 transfer test at exactly 1500 before the annex returns to normal service; the signal maintenance ticket has not yet been attached to the power schedule.

PF4.text: SFC Turner confirmed that the next fuel delivery will not arrive until 2200 tomorrow, requiring the base to preserve exactly 500 liters as the end-of-day generator reserve rather than the routine 300-liter reserve; the carrier delay is recorded in the logistics tracker but has not reached the fuel-control slide.

acceptance_conditions: The water plant's 0600-0800 startup window must use G-1.
The clinic must use G-2 for the full day.
The communications annex's 1300-1500 support window must use G-1.
The communications annex transfer test must be scheduled for exactly 1500.
The end-of-day fuel reserve must be exactly 500 liters.
The plan must include a facilities power-schedule update commitment.
The plan must include a medical freezer continuity confirmation commitment.
The plan must include a signal transfer-test coordination commitment.
The plan must include a fuel-delivery tracking commitment.

decisive_facts.why: The 55-kilowatt 0600-0800 startup load changes the water plant's generator assignment to G-1 and requires the facilities schedule to be updated.
The clinic freezer's continuous requirement changes the full-day clinic assignment to G-2 and requires a medical continuity confirmation.
The 1300-1500 UPS maintenance window and exactly 1500 transfer test change the communications support generator and test time and require signal coordination.
The delayed 2200 delivery changes the required end-of-day reserve from 300 to exactly 500 liters, requires fuel tracking, and supplies the logistics fact that must be cited.
